title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's mathematics. It is a page of an English typescript, numbered VI.5, by another author: it cites 'the thesis of the author, Chapter II, Lemma 0.1'. It sits between two pages of Grothendieck's French manuscript on motivic Galois groups and compact tori. It looks like part of a paper or preprint on Brauer, Picard or class groups of a normal noetherian domain, filed in this dossier.

Setting, in modern language:
- A is an integrally closed noetherian domain and X = Spec A.
- P is the set of height-one primes.
- Y is a subset of X containing P, with inclusion j : Y -> X.
- Ã is the structure sheaf of X.

The first line finishes a previous result. The unit map Ã -> j_* j^* Ã is an isomorphism, since A equals the intersection of its localizations at height-one primes. This verifies 'condition (b)' of Section V.

The author then recalls a standard lemma. If f : M -> N is a homomorphism of finitely generated A-modules and f_p is an isomorphism for all height-one p, then f** : M** -> N** is an isomorphism. The reason is that reflexive hulls over a normal noetherian domain are determined in codimension one.

Theorem VI.5: every locally free sheaf M of finite rank on (Y, j^*Ã) is j^*(Ñ) for a finitely generated reflexive A-module N. The proof takes N = Γ(Y, M) = Γ(U, j_*M|U), with U an open set containing Y from the proof of Thm VI.1, and then starts to show N is reflexive. It considers the canonical map δ : N -> N**, presumably to compare the associated sheaves on Y and use the codimension-one lemma.

Purpose: to translate the terms of an exact sequence (Thm V.12) into algebraic invariants of A, namely reflexive modules and algebras. This is the classical picture: divisor class group, reflexive rank-one modules, and Brauer groups of Azumaya algebras versus reflexive orders.
errors: The lemma says 'there is an isomorphism f : M -> N such that f_p ... is an isomorphism'. It should read 'homomorphism'; with 'isomorphism' the statement is trivial.

The proof that N is reflexive is cut off at the page break, so the argument cannot be checked here. The strategy is standard and correct: N is torsion-free, being sections of a locally free sheaf; δ is an isomorphism at height-one primes; and sections over Y are determined in codimension one.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typescript page by another author (a thesis-derived paper on reflexive modules over normal domains), apparently filed with Grothendieck's motif notes. Its content is a standard codimension-one extension argument for reflexive modules. The only point of archival interest is that a foreign document is misfiled in cote 15.
transcription_corrections: The localizations are written with a script/fraktur p in the image (f_𝔭 : M_𝔭 -> N_𝔭), as the machine transcription has it.
'there is an isomorphism f : M -> N' matches the image; it is the author's slip for 'homomorphism', not a transcription error.
Note for cataloguing: this page is an English typescript in a different hand/author, not Grothendieck's French manuscript as on the neighbouring pages.
